//: lib: ["ES2019", "ESNext.Iterator"] is the floor this package actually needs, and two identifiers set it. ES2019 comes from Object.fromEntries (obj.ts, and flattenMap.ts through it) -- verified ES2018 and ES2017 fail on exactly that one (TS2550, 'try changing lib to es2019 or later'), and ES2015 additionally fails on Object.values/Object.entries (ES2017). The ESNext.Iterator sliver comes from Iterator.from, the ES2025 iterator helper entry point, called by iterable.ts's isAllThere, concat, zip and sequenceEquals -- verified ES2019 alone fails on exactly those four call sites (TS2693, 'Iterator only refers to a type, but is being used as a value here'). No ES-numbered lib bundles that helper yet, hence the sliver rather than a bump to a numbered year; the IteratorObject in concat's return type needs none of it, being declared in lib.es2015.iterable. Nothing else here reaches past lib.es2015.iterable (Iterable, Symbol.iterator) and lib.es5; the two workspace dependencies clear this floor themselves -- @rhombus-toolkit/types is at ES2018 and @rhombus-toolkit/type-guards, which supplies isFunction and isIterable, is too. No DOM: nothing here names a DOM identifier. types: [] is inherited from tsconfig.lib.json and stays -- the runtime spec below is excluded rather than given @types/bun, so no ambient package can quietly loosen this floor. exclude: the *.spec.ts runtime tests belong to `bun test`, not to the library program.
